inputs.text: Earlier this month, an Indiana judge blocked a prolife law after the ACLU and Hoosier Jews for Choice argued that it burdened religious freedom by limiting access to abortion. The message calls this an inversion: a principle meant to protect belief is being used to weaken abortion limits, presented in neutral legal language. It says LifeNews’s headline signals which side it believes is benefiting, while the framing itself is part of the contest over who gets to define religious freedom.

output.main_topic: Indiana judge blocks prolife law after religious-freedom challenge
